text:
A dreaming of the pale branches

and the plains where wheat sets,

a breathing toward solitude with you

through the damp valleys and the woodland:


a seeking of the deep and savage region,

a desire to possess you without witness,

an embraced longing to be with myself

seeing your face in an inner landscape:


such was my truest youth;

in the ideal climate of your sweetness

my divine spring matured:


and I held my hope so certain,

as though in passing beauty

your beauty gave itself to me, intact.

translation.title: A Dreaming of the Pale Branches
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the sonnet's inward landscape of desire, solitude, and intact beauty.
